dataset.description: The dataset will be generated through the annual Baltic Individual Crisis Preparedness Barometer surveys conducted across eight Baltic Sea Region countries. It captures individuals’ threat perceptions, crisis preparedness behaviors, psychological factors, communication influences, and governance-related aspects.

distribution.title:
The primary purpose of the data collection is to generate annual, comparable, multi‑country evidence on individuals’ threat perceptions, crisis preparedness behaviors, and the psychological, communication, and governance factors that influence them. This dataset is essential for meeting the project’s objectives: to institutionalize the Baltic Individual Crisis Preparedness Barometer, track preparedness trends across eight Baltic Sea Region countries, and provide policymakers with actionable insights for strengthening civil resilience. 
By collecting these data annually, the project supports the development of evidence‑based communication strategies, preparedness campaigns, and policy recommendations for governments, municipalities, EU bodies, and regional organizations. The dataset also contributes to the University of Latvia’s goal of becoming a regional hub for crisis‑preparedness research and high‑impact data.

dataset.title: Survey results of the Baltic Sea region

dmp.description:
The Baltic Individual Crisis Preparedness Barometer project generates annual, multi‑country survey data on threat perception, crisis readiness, and related psychological, communication, and governance dimensions across eight Baltic Sea Region countries. As the project aims to institutionalize a recurring, high‑impact dataset for policymakers, researchers, and practitioners, systematic data management is essential to ensure the reliability, continuity, and long‑term usability of the Barometer.
The purpose of the DMP is to outline how all project data—survey datasets, analytical outputs, documentation, and derived materials—will be collected, stored, processed, protected, shared, and preserved throughout the 2026–2029 project period and beyond. It ensures compliance with ethical standards, GDPR, and University of Latvia policies, while enabling secure cross-institutional collaboration with partners such as the Council of the Baltic Sea States, national authorities, and academic institutions. The DMP also supports sustainability by establishing procedures for long‑term data stewardship, facilitating annual replication of the Barometer, and enabling future scaling to EU‑wide initiatives.
